actions.label: Compare direct and remapped context-menu input

comment.body: Which application and focused control shows the menu at the top-left? In that same control, please compare pressing Shift+F10 directly with your Copilot-to-Shift+F10 remap, keeping the same item focused. If you have an Apps/Menu key, its result is a useful separate comparison: that key is not the same input as the shortcut currently configured. This will distinguish an input-state difference introduced by the remap from the application choosing the same menu position for direct input. Please preserve your other mappings.

verification: In the affected control the supported remap produces the same menu placement as the intended direct input.
Win and Shift are not left logically pressed after the remap; ordinary shortcuts remain intact.
Compare Explorer and the affected application, including keyboard-focused versus mouse-focused items; retain application-specific behavior.
plan: Record the application and exact focused control, then compare direct Shift+F10 with the Copilot-to-Shift+F10 remap without changing focus.
Use a direct Apps/Menu key as a separate control where available; do not assume it is the same input contract as Shift+F10.
If only the remap differs, trace injected modifier down/up state and focus delivery; correct that demonstrated boundary without forcing global cursor coordinates.

confidence.rationale: The mapping and observed location are explicit, but the receiving application and direct-input baseline are missing.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unverified hypotheses: the receiving control may place direct Shift+F10 at the same origin, or the remap may deliver a different modifier/focus state. The missing application comparison determines which path applies.
proposed_fixes.title: Isolate context-menu positioning after Copilot shortcut remapping

judgment.recommended_action: Identify the receiving application/control and compare direct versus remapped Shift+F10 in that same focus state.
evidence: The0.97.1report specifies a shortcut-to-shortcut mapping from LeftWin+LeftShift+F23 to LeftShift+F10 and observes a context menu at the upper-left of the screen.
The expected behavior refers to a focused item or mouse position, but no target application/control or focus state is given.
There are no discussion replies, attachments or linked implementation in the saved complete context. The configured output is a Shift+F10 shortcut, not the distinct Apps/Menu virtual key.
judgment.rationale: Menu positioning is determined by the receiving application as well as input state. Compare direct Shift+F10 with remapped Shift+F10 in the same focused control before attributing the position to Keyboard Manager or assuming the Apps key and shortcut are identical. A modifier-release regression remains a hypothesis, not a measured cause.

fix_assessment.rationale: A targeted input/focus comparison can isolate a mapping-specific regression, but the report does not yet establish a failing event producer or application behavior.

inferences: A keyboard shortcut can invoke a menu without supplying the mouse position; a screen-origin menu alone does not establish which component lost the intended anchor.
